public_rationale: Marcus offers a qualified judgment that his prediction was largely vindicated and explicitly concedes a timing error. Scoring this requires deciding what partial correctness means and how attack size should be measured. His words supply neither rule. A strict record-scale test would remove the qualification; allowing an arbitrary shortfall would invent a concession. The incident report provides context but cannot settle that judgment. This classification neither validates nor refutes the underlying prediction.
limitations: The original Politico text was inaccessible.
No historical ranking of the Optimizely incident is asserted.
The obstacle is the undefined standard of partial vindication, not merely incomplete incident reporting.
